solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Steadfast continuation through divorce

parts.note: per means through or by way of, as in 'per post'
a divorce is a severance of a marriage

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going doggedly even while their marriage is breaking up.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistence is a steadfast carrying-on in spite of difficulty, a synonym for the clue's phrase.

clue.text: Alec's reviewed schedule about moving staircase

indicators.note: reviewed read as re-viewed, looked at afresh in a new order, so the letters of Alec's are rearranged
about here means turned round, so the word for schedule is written backwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: Alec checks over a timetable concerning a moving staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges ALECS into ESCAL; 'about' turns ROTA into ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A powered stairway that carries people up or down is the standard description of this machine.

clue.text: Skin infection cases spread around British island

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the two-letter piece
spread around suggests the letters of cases are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Cases of a skin infection have spread around a British island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges CASES into SCAES, which goes 'around' BI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an itchy contagious skin condition caused by mites burrowing under the skin.

clue.text: Old authoress from eastern US state with predatory canine, we hear

parts.note: Virginia is a state on the US east coast

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for the animal is to be taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: a wolf is a predatory wild dog

explanation.surface: An old woman writer comes from the eastern United States with a hunting dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' means WOLF is spoken, giving the novelist's surname spelt WOOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: The modernist novelist of Mrs Dalloway died in 1941, so she is a female author of the past.

clue.text: Run by Russian river in the countryside

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the Ural is a river flowing through Russia

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a run beside a Russian river out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for things of farmland and villages, the opposite of urban.

clue.text: Arrest northern seaman

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: Police detain a sailor from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang verb meaning to catch or seize a suspect.

clue.text: Extremely alert entering weird cafe perhaps

indicators.note: entering means the picked letters go inside the word for weird

parts.note: eery is a variant spelling of eerie, meaning weird

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extreme letters, first and last, of the word alert

explanation.surface: Someone very watchful walks into a strange cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym, using the rarer spelling of eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe is one example of a place to eat; 'perhaps' marks it as one instance of the broader term.

clue.text: Split cents remaining

parts.note: left means remaining, as in 'two biscuits left'

explanation.surface: The few cents that are left over get divided up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something divided or cracked apart, as in a split chin.

clue.text: Elastic material seen in lovely craftwork

indicators.note: seen in means the answer can be spotted running through the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A stretchy fabric is used in some attractive handicraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The trademark stretch fibre used in sportswear is a type of elastic fabric.

clue.text: Cheesy food, undercooked, cut using teeth

parts.note: rare meat is lightly cooked, still red inside
bit is the past tense of bite, to cut with the teeth

explanation.surface: Some cheese dish, not cooked enough, is bitten into.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of melted cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is a cheese sauce grilled on toast, so food that is cheesy in the literal sense.

clue.text: Italian filmmaker collapsed in middle of musical

parts.note: fell means collapsed or fell down

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of the seven-letter word musical

explanation.surface: An Italian director collapsed halfway through a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico of La Dolce Vita was a celebrated director from Italy.

clue.text: Delay Cockney lady's alcoholic drink

parts.note: a lag is a delay, as in time lag
a Cockney drops the h, so a lady's thing is 'er, short for her

explanation.surface: A Londoner's woman is slow to get her drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop the H, so 'her' becomes 'er.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, fizzy beer is a common example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Fellow frauds concealing wife, a conspirator once

parts.note: guy is an informal word for a fellow or man

indicators.note: concealing means the word for frauds hides the letter for wife inside it

parts.note: fakes are frauds or impostors

explanation.surface: A man's deceptions hide his wife, who plotted with him.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes was in the 1605 Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament, remembered on Bonfire Night in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: He was one of the Catholic plotters of 1605, so a historical conspirator.

clue.text: Trial, in my opinion, primarily needs youth's evidence

parts.note: a test is a trial
IMO is the texting abbreviation for in my opinion

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letters of the following two words

explanation.surface: At a trial, someone feels a young person's statement is chiefly what's needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness's sworn statement in court counts as evidence.

clue.text: In the open air, beat gold

parts.note: to outdo someone is to beat them
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Beating gold out of doors, like a smith working outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for things done outside rather than within a building.

clue.text: Impish person confused priest

indicators.note: confused means the letters of priest are mixed up into another order

explanation.surface: A mischievous character has bewildered a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf or fairy, a mischievous small spirit, is a kind of impish being.

clue.text: Son, in front of children, slides uncontrollably

indicators.note: in front of places the letter for son before the word for children

parts.note: kids are children

explanation.surface: A boy ahead of the other children slips and slides out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle or person losing grip and sliding on a surface is said to do this.

clue.text: Mother goes after standard type of ham

indicators.note: goes after puts the word for mother behind the word for standard

parts.note: par is the standard level, as in golf
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum is chasing a regular sort of ham.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured ham from the Italian city of that name is a well-known variety.

clue.text: In the morning, bishop maybe somewhere in Jordan

parts.note: AM is ante meridiem, before noon
a bishop is one example of a chess piece, or man

explanation.surface: A clergyman travels in the morning to a Jordanian location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop' is not the cleric but a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Jordan, so certainly a place in that country.

clue.text: Medical wrapping we fasten to maintain pressure

indicators.note: to maintain means to hold, so the word for fasten holds the pressure letter inside

parts.note: to tack is to fasten, as with a small nail or loose stitches
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Nurses tie a medical dressing to keep pressure on a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp cloth wrapped round a patient as treatment is a kind of medical wrap.

clue.text: Up in the air during dance

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
the limbo is a Caribbean dance under a lowered bar

explanation.surface: Someone is high in the air while dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for being undecided or in a state of uncertainty.

clue.text: Circuit of track friend recalled

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the word for friend is written backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend remembers a circuit of the running track.
explanation.definitionFit: One complete trip round a racetrack is the usual sense of the word.

clue.text: Agreed to restrain a newsman describing certain wines

indicators.note: to restrain means to hold in, so the agreement word holds the a inside

parts.note: OK means agreed
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword newsman

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to hold back a journalist writing tasting notes on wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Wines matured in wooden barrels take on that timber's flavour, so the word describes such wines.

clue.text: Fingerpost repositioned after recording English woodland area

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters come behind the recording

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: repositioned means the letters of fingerpost are put in new places

explanation.surface: A signpost was moved after a recording was made in a woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repositioned' rearranges FINGERPOST into PINGFOREST. Epping Forest is ancient woodland on London's north-east edge in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large ancient forest in England, so an English wooded area.
